messages:
jamie: Heads-up — I want to propose a two-stage plan to promote telemetry.route_info (jsonb) to a first-class route_profile table and column set in analytics. Reason: ORMs and dashboard queries are suffering from jsonb extraction at scale; high p99 on console queries and per-route quota calc is expensive. Sketch below.

ravi: :thumbsup: outline pls (tl;dr)

jamie: Short version: 1) Shadow-write new normalized table (route_profiles) + route_profile_id on events; 2) Read adapter: prefer normalized but fallback to jsonb; 3) Backfill historical data in batches; 4) Cutover with feature flag and migration metrics.

sara: Thoughts on schema? tenant-scoped is safer. I vote for (tenant_id, route_hash, profile_version) as composite key. Avoid relying on route_name strings.

matt: Concern: backfill cost. Rehydrating from raw events is O(10s TB). Can we compute profiles from daily aggregates instead? Also need explicit indexes on (tenant_id, route_hash) and a partial index for active routes.

leo: Console UX note — during migration dashboards could show mixed rows. Add migration_status and expose a small 'use-new-profiles' toggle in the console so SEs can flip per-workspace. Also surface a 'migration-coverage' metric.

jamie: Proposed DDL snippet:
```sql
CREATE TABLE analytics.route_profiles (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id UUID NOT NULL,
  route_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  profile_version INT DEFAULT 1,
  params JSONB,
  computed_quota_units BIGINT,
  migration_status TEXT DEFAULT 'shadow',
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX ON analytics.route_profiles (tenant_id, route_hash);
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN route_profile_id BIGINT;
-- shadow write: write both events.route_info -> route_profiles and keep jsonb
```

ravi: Add read-adapter pseudo code:
```
if event.route_profile_id != null:
  return fetch(route_profiles, id)
else:
  return extract_from(event.route_info_jsonb)
```

sara: Metrics to add: read_adapter.miss_count, backfill.rows_processed, backfill.bytes, dashboard.query_p99_before/after. Alert if read_adapter.miss_rate > 5% or query_p99 regresses > 25%.

deploy-bot: migration-canary job queued: canary-run-2026-03-22. ETA ~2h :robot_face:

matt: Also add throttles per-tenant during backfill. Make the backfill checkpointed so we can resume and show progress in the console.

jamie: Timeline idea: week1 shadow-write + internal canary; week2 backfill low-traffic tenants; week3 stagger higher; week4 soft-cutover behind console toggle; week5 full-cutover and jsonb cleanup after 90d. Thoughts?

ravi: Automated cutover ok but require manual approval for top-10 tenants. Also add cost cap check so backfill won't exceed daily egress/cost budget.

sara: Agree. Also plan for rollback: a simple toggle to prefer legacy jsonb if we detect >1% data mismatch in canary queries.

jamie: I'll draft the full playbook and DDL today. @ravi @sara please review indexes and alert thresholds by EOD. Thanks :raised_hands:

matt: :+1:

leo: :eyes:
